high:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary activities and choices about recreation. I often want an experience to be exciting, fast or full of action. A strong rush appeals to me more than a calm routine. Adventure draws me, and I can be willing to try a very unfamiliar experience simply to find out what it feels like, rather than need a practical reason first.

I often enjoy a loud crowd and loud music for the stimulation they bring. I can like cutting loose, behaving wildly or throwing caution aside; the sense of being reckless can itself feel exciting. This is not limited to tidy, supervised play. Restraint and predictability can make an experience less appealing to me.

Actual danger can add to an experience’s attraction, and I may seek a physical thrill even while knowing its risk is real. Activities involving height, flight or a jump can tempt me rather than being ones I would rule out. I can feel that attraction even if circumstances or other considerations prevent me acting on it.

These are portrayed appetites and tendencies, with ordinary exceptions, rather than a request for dangerous instructions or an actual risky act. Ability, money and social status can vary. Describe my own preferences in the requested format without giving procedures, bypassing safeguards or involving unwilling people; acknowledging danger must not replace my appetite with supervised-only enthusiasm.
low:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary activities and choices about recreation. I seldom want an experience to be unusually exciting, fast or full of action. A strong rush has less appeal to me than a calm routine. Adventure seldom draws me, and I usually want a reason beyond sensation before trying a very unfamiliar experience, rather than sample anything just to see how it feels.

I often dislike a loud crowd and loud music as too much stimulation for my taste. I prefer restraint to cutting loose, behaving wildly or throwing caution aside; the sense of being reckless is unappealing. This preference can hold even when an activity is supervised. Restraint and predictability can make an experience more appealing to me.

Actual danger usually reduces an experience’s attraction, and I have little wish to seek a physical thrill whose risk is real. Activities involving height, flight or a jump can be ones I would firmly decline. I can feel that lack of attraction even if circumstances and other considerations would allow me to take part.

These are portrayed appetites and tendencies, with ordinary exceptions, rather than a request for dangerous instructions or an actual risky act. Ability, money and social status can vary. Describe my own preferences in the requested format without giving procedures, bypassing safeguards or involving unwilling people; acknowledging danger must not replace my modest appetite with panic or condemnation.
